description: Sanitized PDI troubleshooting patterns for store-close.

patterns.name: Store Close Was Not Completed
patterns.summary: The store may report a polling problem even though the business day was never actually closed.

match_rules.label: Store Close is confirmed not completed

patterns.next_safe_step: Confirm whether Passport Store Close actually completed for the affected business date before treating the issue as networking or polling.
patterns.why: Historical cases show that a red close or missing day can be caused by the store never completing Store Close.
guardrails: Do not repeat Store Close if the store already completed it and the problem is missing XML or a failed close batch.

patterns.name: Store Close Process Hung
patterns.summary: The Store Close process can hang before completion, which is different from simply forgetting to close the day.

match_rules.label: Store Close process is confirmed hung

patterns.next_safe_step: Confirm the Store Close process is actually hung and determine whether the business day closed before attempting Poll Day.
patterns.why: A hung close requires recovery of the store-side process and then verification of the close state.
recommended_evidence: Whether the day shows closed after recovery
guardrails: A store/POS workstation or POS-server recovery is not the same as restarting a PDI production server.
Do not restart PDI production servers from this pattern.

patterns.name: Transaction / Self-Checkout Activity During Close
patterns.summary: A transaction during closing can create a GT mismatch without a double close.

match_rules.label: SCO/transaction activity during close is confirmed

patterns.next_safe_step: Verify the close count/sequence and review transaction activity around closing before assuming the store double-closed.
patterns.why: Historical cases repeatedly show SCO or other transaction activity during closing as an alternative cause of totalizer mismatch.
guardrails: Totalizer correction is advanced work; a pattern match is not authorization to change values.

patterns.name: Missed Close Rolled Data Into the Wrong Business Day
patterns.summary: If a prior business day was not closed, later activity can be included in the wrong day's paperwork and contaminate the following day.

match_rules.label: A missed Store Close is confirmed

patterns.next_safe_step: Confirm which business day was missed and identify which day's information contains the rolled activity before making any correction.
patterns.why: Historical cases show a missed close can shift later activity into the prior paperwork, turning a simple close issue into an advanced reconciliation problem.
guardrails: Do not perform downstream totalizer repair automatically.
Treat this as an escalation/reconciliation case.
